newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel keeps base rate at 15.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel keeps base rate at 15.2 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said on Monday its key lending rate would remain in December at the current annualised rate of 15.2 percent.

The rate is the one charged commercial banks at daily and weekly monetary tenders. The central bank raised interest rates in the first half of the year, but from August to November it lowered the short-term base rate a total 1.8 percentage points. In each of the previous two months, the bank lowered rates by 0.3 point.
Israeli financial markets had been predicting a reduction of 0.2-0.5 percentage points.

The Bank of Israel said in a statement economic indicators had not changed significantly from the previous month: "Caution is now required in interest rate policy, both against the background of a big budget deficit and the related deficit in the balance of payments," the bank said.

The bank said its policies had brought down inflationary expectations in the bond market close to the 8-10 percent target set by the government and brought the annualised rate down from the approximately 14 percent level experienced in the first half. It said money supply was growing at appropriate levels.
The market's inflationary expectations have been falling since the end of October. Today, they point to a rise of approximately 10.2 percent in consumer prices over the next 12 months.
Nevertheless, the bank said expectations still reflect a rate in excess of the target.
